method: Current USITC/CBSA/Finance legal schedules and effective overlays are represented in the model by the Bank of Canada's current goods-only effective-rate benchmark; tariff-relevant model sectors are agriculture/forestry/fishing, mining/energy and manufacturing.

method: Use the Department of Finance reported share of Canadian exports covered by the then-applicable broad US tariffs that were CUSMA-compliant and entered duty-free as the current high-level compliance proxy.
notes: Statistics Canada Q4-2025 CUSMA compliance/certification tables are retained as an independent industry-level provenance source; this is a compliance proxy, not a customs-entry utilization microstatistic.

method: Gravity estimates from 60 importers, 207 exporters and 23 tradable sectors. Sector 0 equally averages published agriculture and fishing estimates; sector 1 uses mining; sector 4 equally averages published manufacturing estimates.
notes: Manufacturing standard error is the standard error of an equal-weight mapped mean using reported component standard errors; miscellaneous manufacturing has no reported SE and contributes zero to that propagation calculation.

method: Bank of Canada difference-in-differences evidence finds tariffed retail prices peaked about 6% above controls under a 25% tariff; 6/25 = 0.24 pass-through.
notes: The public research summary does not report a single aggregate standard error for the 0.24 mapping, so no false precision is supplied.
